text:
maya: Heads-up: bringing up yukari-v0.8-q6 on canary for multilingual smoke. Quick run on the vertical-JP+AR subset shows some strange ruby (furigana) tokens getting attached to surrounding Arabic when documents contain inline Arabic in captions. BLEU/chrF dropped on the mixed-vertical subset by ~1.8.
sahil: hmm that sounds odd. vertical jp + arabic together isn't a common combo in our corpora. can you paste a failing example?
mei: also which quant path and tokenizer version? we recently switched to fast-tokenizer v4 in prod canaries.
maya: quant=q6 (hybrid int6 path), tokenizer=fast-v4, normalization=unicode-nfkc+custom-ruby. sample input (rendered multi-line):
```
[vertical block]
漢字(かんじ)︱嵐の歌
caption: بالعربية: هذا اختبار (note: inline Arabic)
---
combined line sent to model as: \nVERTICAL_START
漢字(かんじ)RUBY_BREAK嵐の歌
CAPTION: بالعربية: هذا اختبار
```
model expected detok: "Kanji (kanji) | Arashi no uta" and "Caption: in Arabic: this is a test"
model observed detok: "Kanji(かんじ)︱3837 text" or sometimes ruby attached to Arabic tokens: "嵐の歌3931"
mei: looks like the detokenizer is not handling vertical ruby markers and then hitting an RTL shaping step that assumes previous codepoint is part of the Arabic run. could be a missing bidi reset after ruby marker.
sahil: check the tokenizer token stream boundaries around the ruby markers. maybe fast-v4's custom-ruby optimization merges the ruby grapheme into the previous token for space efficiency.
maya: repro command I used (canary):
```bash
PYTHONPATH=./tools python tests/repro_vertical.py \
  --model yukari-v0.8-q6 --subset vertical_jp_ar --no-batch --seed 11 \
  --tokenizer fast-v4 --tokenizer-debug true > /tmp/yukari_vq6_vert.out
# output: /tmp/yukari_vq6_vert.out
```
mei: nice. can you attach the tokenized lines (token ids + raw unicode) from the debug dump? if we can see when the ruby marker ID merges with arabic cluster it's clearer.
eval-bot: quick metrics snapshot (vertical_jp_ar subset): BLEU_base=34.5 -> BLEU_canary=32.7, chrF=0.64 -> 0.62, token-boundary-failures=0.9% -> 2.4%
ci-bot: note: fast-v4 tokenizer rollout was gated but allowed on canary via feature-flag TK_FAST_V4=true in canary pool.
sahil: if the ruby optimizer is aggressively coalescing subtokens across script boundaries we need a rule: never coalesce across strong bidi class changes (e.g., L to AL/AN). That should prevent Arabic from inheriting ruby suffixes.
mei: agreed. short-term mitigation: flip TK_FAST_V4 feature-flag off for canary pool or disable custom-ruby optimization. Which is quicker?
maya: disabling the ruby optimization in the tokenizer config is a one-line flip and doesn't require model re-push. i'll flip and rerun repro.
sahil: also pls open a small unit test that includes: vertical ruby + inline Arabic + bracket pairs to ensure bidi resets. put it under tests/tokenizer_unit/test_mixed_vertical_ruby.py
mei: I'll audit the detok bidi post-processing too; there might be a missing U+061C or LRM insertion in our detok pipeline.
maya: flip done. running repro now. will post before/after token diffs.
eval-bot: after-rollback snapshot (prelim): BLEU_canary=33.9, chrF=0.635, token-boundary-failures=1.1% (improvement). full run pending.
sahil: if rollback fixes it, we should add the rule in tokenization: block ruby-coalesce across different script-type boundaries OR across bidi-class changes. also record in onboarding checklist: "vertical+rtl smoke".
mei: filing followups: TICKET-ml-789: tokenizer ruby coalesce audit; TICKET-ml-790: detok bidi reset fix; TICKET-ml-791: add unit + corpus sample.
maya: assigning owners: sahil (coalesce rule + PR), mei (detok audit + test), maya (canary retest + ticket writeups). tagging @eng-ml for visibility.
mei: i'll run a broader smoke on mixed-orient subset after canary finishes to ensure no regressions elsewhere.
maya: thanks everyone. will update thread with final numbers and attach debug snippets. :white_check_mark:
